title: GS21 industry sign x financial leverage: two industries (gs_level 0.8 / 1.2) x three fixed coupons (0.15 / 0.40 / 0.70), production exposure sign x 0.15 x coupon/0.40 = [-0.0562, -0.15, -0.2625, 0.0562, 0.15, 0.2625], value-compensated, price 2.5
question: Does an interaction with a plain story -- industries on opposite sides of a priced shock, the levered firm's cash flow moving more -- give GS21 room and a fair gap at the bar (+0.029), with leverage and size observed and industry not?
notes:
WHY (2026-11-01, interpretable interactions). The interaction economies share a frame (a priced shock with winners and losers by industry, the sign only partly revealed by size, times a firm-level amplifier) and differ in the amplifier: BGN bvychs35 the assets-in-place share (emergent), KP14 vygelbcs the profitability deviation, GS21 gvysz the productivity. The most natural amplifier is FINANCIAL LEVERAGE: with debt service fixed and no hedging capacity, the levered firm's cash flow is more exposed to the shock. GS21 is the model with debt; gvyzlf's fixed-coupon chassis gives leverage a real cross-section (endogenous leverage spans 0.002-0.006 across quintiles). Two industries (sign -1 at gs_level 0.8, +1 at 1.2: industries differ in scale, so size partly reveals the sign) x three coupons; the production-level exposure is sign x 0.15 x coupon/0.40 = [-0.0562, -0.15, -0.2625, 0.0562, 0.15, 0.2625]; bv_comp 1.0 compensates the y = 0 value per unit perpetuity (long-run entry). The econometrician's linear model in (size, book-to-market, asset growth, ROE, momentum, leverage) cannot represent sign(size) x leverage; random features can.

PREDICTION (2026-11-01): room 40% or more (a product of two visible, mean-zero factors: gvyp15's 0.25 absolute room came from productivity x coupon with far less leverage dispersion) and a fair gap of +0.03 to +0.10. FALSIFIED if room is at or below 15% on three seeds, or the most levered exposed firms select themselves out of the panel (gvytls).
